title: Drive Radio — August 11, 2026
description:
- North Korean remote IT staffer worked for US government agency, says FBI: A North Korean operative reportedly landed a contractor role inside a US government agency, exposing how outsourced hiring pipelines can be exploited for sanctions evasion. (https://techcrunch.com/2026/08/11/north-korean-remote-it-staffer-worked-for-us-government-agency-says-fbi/)
- Bumble ditches its rule that kept men from making the first move: Bumble is abandoning the women-message-first rule that defined its brand since launch, as growth pressure reshapes dating app design. (https://techcrunch.com/2026/08/11/bumble-ditches-its-rule-that-kept-men-from-making-the-first-move/)
- Mark Zuckerberg attacks 'closed' AI rivals as Meta returns to open models: Meta reverses course again, going back to open-weight AI and dropping the massive local-agent model Muse Glimmer to challenge closed rivals. (https://www.ft.com/content/4e3957f8-ea7c-4c46-a3de-cdce8e526878)
- Anthropic says it will watermark text generated by its AI models: Anthropic is rolling out watermarking for Claude's text output, a much harder technical problem than watermarking images, amid rising pressure to label AI content. (https://techcrunch.com/2026/08/11/anthropic-says-it-will-watermark-text-generated-by-its-ai-models/)
- As AI eats the web, the internet's collective memory is disappearing: AI summaries are replacing search clicks, starving smaller websites of traffic and quietly erasing chunks of the web's history. (https://thewalrus.ca/google-search-is-dying/)
- France to ban unsolicited telemarketing calls: France is enacting a flat-out ban on cold-call telemarketing starting August 11th, closing loopholes that made earlier do-not-call rules toothless. (https://www.lemonde.fr/en/france/article/2026/08/06/france-to-ban-unsolicited-telemarketing-calls-from-august-11_6756208_7.html)
- Jeff Bezos might finally get his hands on a sports team: Bezos is reportedly closing in on a stake in Liverpool FC, joining the wave of American tech money buying into English football's media empire. (https://techcrunch.com/2026/08/10/jeff-bezos-might-finally-get-his-hands-on-a-sports-team/)

title: Drive Radio — August 7, 2026
description:
- Mario Meets Pareto: A deep dive showing how a tiny fraction of Super Mario Bros.' design decisions create almost all the fun — a masterclass in doing less but better. (https://www.mayerowitz.io/blog/mario-meets-pareto)
- AMD acquires Taalas to etch AI models directly into silicon: AMD's latest acquisition bets that some AI models are stable and popular enough to be baked permanently into chips for blazing-fast, ultra-efficient inference. (https://www.theregister.com/systems/2026/08/06/amd-acquires-ai-chip-startup-taalas-to-boost-inference-performance-by-etching-models-into-silicon/5284344)
- GitHub Actions and Pages are experiencing degraded availability: Another GitHub outage takes down developer workflows worldwide, a reminder of how much of the internet quietly depends on one company's uptime. (https://www.githubstatus.com/incidents/qcvjkzcs7j74)
- Humans missed 1 in 3 threats approving AI agent commands across 40k game runs: A sobering study shows human 'oversight' of AI agents is often just rubber-stamping — with real security risk as agents get more autonomy. (https://scalex.dev/blog/ai-agent-permissions-stats/)
- Quake – 30th Anniversary Update: The game that helped launch consumer 3D graphics cards just turned 30 and got fresh content — a fun look back at gaming history. (https://slayersclub.bethesda.net/en-US/news/quake-30th-anniversary-update)
- Meta Ordered to Pay $942M to Address Harm to Kids from Social Media: A near-billion-dollar ruling tied to Meta's own internal research on teen mental health raises the question of whether fines actually change behavior. (https://www.wsj.com/tech/meta-ordered-to-pay-942-million-to-address-harm-to-kids-from-social-media-8ba5aab7)
- My phone detects going on a run as 'someone snatching my phone and running off': A hilarious real-world example of AI safety features failing for anyone outside their narrow training assumptions. (https://mastodon.gamedev.place/@rygorous/117047697255584965)

title: Drive Radio — August 6, 2026
description:
- Elon Musk's AI Wikipedia hasn't been updated in months: Grokipedia was pitched as a 'living' AI-powered rival to Wikipedia but has been completely frozen for over three months. (https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/976004/elon-musk-grokipedia-ai-wikipedia-not-updating-dead)
- Changes at Google DeepMind: Hassabis to Chair, Jeff Dean departs: A leadership reshuffle at the top of Google's AI empire, with a legendary engineer walking out the door entirely. (https://blog.google/company-news/inside-google/message-ceo/next-chapter-ai-momentum/)
- Nashville uses eminent domain to block data center near zoo: A city government flips eminent domain on its head, using it to stop a data center instead of build one. (https://www.costar.com/article/970809918/nashville-council-approves-eminent-domain-action-to-halt-data-center-project)
- Sure seems like Fenix Flexin used AI music generator Treblo: A viral hit song gets outed as AI-made by the very company whose tool made it, kicking off a new era of music forensics. (https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/975528/fenix-flexin-ai-music-generator-treblo)
- SpaceX is barely Space and mostly X: SpaceX's first combined earnings report reveals it's now primarily a telecom and AI-compute business, not a rocket company. (https://www.theverge.com/science/975545/spacex-x-earnings-ai-data-centers-compute-space)
